rulings.challenge_claim: The row slices at a verse carrying an undisclosed ketiv/qere note, and it calls the cited neighbour verse unmarked while that verse carries one too.
rulings.grounds: Both arms verify from the bytes. The staged variant inventory records exactly one note inside Jer.15.5-Jer.15.9, at MT 15:9 -- the row's own terminal verse and the verse its closing argument rests on -- and the doubled reading stands in the bytes as the unpointed ketiv beside the pointed qere, באה בָּ֥א (oshb:Jer.15.9, byte tier); MT 15:5-15:8 carry none (sweep: 0 notes across those four verses), so the omission is the whole in-span obligation. The neighbour arm holds too: MT 15:4 carries no parashah mark but does carry one variant note, לזועה לְזַֽעֲוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.15.4, byte tier), so calling that verse unmarked is true of the parashah layer alone and false of the mark inventory read whole. Parashah handling is otherwise complete and correctly typed (1 marked verse in MT 15:5-15:9, the setumah at MT 15:9; tier-3 weak corroboration in the Prophets, single-witness). No splice runs through either doubled reading and the seam is untouched, so this is a disclosure defect, not a boundary defect. The two arms are unequal -- the neighbour sentence is a precision failure inside a parashah statement, while the in-span note is an outright omission in a verse the row both cuts at and argues from -- and the stated severity survives that split.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add the single-witness ketiv/qere disclosure for MT 15:9, naming the doubled reading, and re-word the Jer.15.4 sentence so it names the layer it speaks for (no parashah mark at MT 15:4) plus that verse's one variant note. Leave span, unit_type, confidence and observed_substrate_signals untouched. Cure test (the test that killed the original): every ketiv/qere verse inside Jer.15.5-Jer.15.9 must be named in device_notes under the single-witness label, and no verse may be called unmarked without naming the layer that word covers.

rulings.challenge_claim: The stated ground for declining a cut at 15:19 is byte-false: the divine reply is not already underway there, because 15:15-18 is the prophet's own voice, so the verse-initial koh-amar does carry a change of speaking mouth; two ketiv/qere notes inside the span are also undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The premise fails on the span's own bytes. The reply opening at MT 15:11 runs to MT 15:14; MT 15:15 turns to the prophet addressing the deity, אַתָּ֧ה יָדַ֣עְתָּ יְהוָ֗ה זָכְרֵ֤נִי וּפָקְדֵ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Jer.15.15, byte tier) -- a vocative divine name standing between a second-person-singular verb and two imperatives carrying first-person-singular object suffixes -- and the first-person complaint holds through MT 15:16-15:18, both witnesses rendering those four verses in the prophet's mouth. So the formula at לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.15.19, byte tier) resumes divine speech after four verses in the other mouth: the mouth carrying the formula does change there, and the row's reason for declining the cut -- that it brings no change of frame-owner from a reply already underway -- is contradicted by the bytes it cites. Under the ruled granularity a koh-amar onset WITH a frame-owner change is a licensed internal seam, so what the row sets aside as a non-event is a live seam candidate. The mark arm verifies as well: two variant notes fall inside Jer.15.10-Jer.15.21, at MT 15:11 -- שרותך שֵֽׁרִיתִ֖יךָ (oshb:Jer.15.11, byte tier), the verse cited as the reply's onset -- and at MT 15:16, inside the complaint; neither is disclosed. Independently re-verified and NOT defective: the row's 8-verse digit for the alef-initial outcry lexeme matches the byte-derived count object exactly (8 verses, MT keys), while a bare consonantal substring sweep on the same three letters returns 14 verses, contaminated by the enemy and fool bases -- the digit is true only under the token-bound object the row names, and it names it. Parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 15:10, 15:14, 15:16, 15:17, 15:18; petuchah at MT 15:21; the two types never conflated). High stands: the defect sits in the clause that carries the row's whole hold-together argument.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative and the matching boundary_rationale clause: rewrite on a true premise -- the divine reply does not run unbroken from 15:11; it breaks at 15:15 where the prophet's voice resumes, and the formula at 15:19 opens a second divine reply with a changed speaking mouth. Any ground for holding Jer.15.10-Jer.15.21 whole must then be argued from the complaint-and-reply exchange as one scene under the frame-plus-speech default-larger-unit rule, not from a continuous reply. device_notes: add the single-witness ketiv/qere disclosure for MT 15:11 and MT 15:16. Splitting at 15:19 is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit owner adoption -- never author work. Cure test: a per-verse mouth check across Jer.15.10-Jer.15.21 must sustain every voice statement the prose makes, and every in-span variant verse must be named.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two stated grounds are byte-contested -- the koh-amar at 16:5 heads the mourning prohibition itself rather than a rationale at 16:6-7, and the span is not addressed to one hearer named in it -- and the parashah-position statement is wrong for the mark at MT 16:4.
rulings.grounds: Two arms verify, one is over-read. Formula location: MT 16:5 puts formula and prohibition in a single verse, כִּֽי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל תָּבוֹא֙ בֵּ֣ית מַרְזֵ֔חַ (oshb:Jer.16.5, byte tier), and MT 16:6-16:7 carry no speech formula at all (sweep: 0 koh-amar verses in MT 16:6-16:7), so pairing the mourning command with a koh-amar rationale at 16:6-7 mislocates the formula; the parallel pairing for the marriage command is right, its formula standing at MT 16:3 with the rationale running to MT 16:4. Mark position: the mark keyed to MT 16:4 stands after that verse, between the marriage command-and-rationale block of 16:2-16:4 and the mourning command at 16:5 -- that is, between two prohibitions -- while only the mark keyed to MT 16:8 falls between a command and its own rationale at 16:9; the row's both is right for one of the two. CORRECTED FINDING on the addressee arm: the name half is true, the prophet's name standing in no verse of chapters 15, 16 or 17 under either attested spelling (token-bound sweeps, MT keys: 109 verses book-wide for the long spelling, 117 verses for any variant, 0 in each of those three chapters), so named is the wrong word; but the conclusion that the one-hearer ground fails outright is over-read. The frame addressee does not change anywhere in the span -- MT 16:2, MT 16:5 and MT 16:8 all carry second-person-singular prohibitions to the one who receives the word at MT 16:1 -- and the plural of MT 16:9, לְעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם וּבִֽימֵיכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.16.9, byte tier), stands inside the quoted oracle content, addressing the people the oracle is about rather than the hearer the commands are given to. The no-scene-change ground therefore survives; only its wording fails. No variant note falls in Jer.16.1-Jer.16.9 (sweep: 0 notes), so nothing is owed on that arm, and the disclosure of the petuchah at MT 15:21 ahead of the opening is correct.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-cut the formula sentence so the mourning command's koh-amar is located at 16:5 with the command and 16:6-7 named as its rationale carrying no formula; replace the clause 'Jeremiah is the one hearer named across the span' with a frame-level statement (the second-person-singular addressee of the commands at 16:2, 16:5 and 16:8 does not change), and keep the second-person-plural of 16:9 disclosed as oracle-internal address rather than a frame addressee. device_notes: replace 'Both interior breaks fall inside a prohibition rather than between two of them' with the per-mark reading -- the mark at MT 16:4 stands between two prohibitions, the mark at MT 16:8 between a command and its rationale. No span change; the seam ground survives, so confidence need not move. Cure test: every formula-location and mark-position sentence must be re-derivable verse by verse from the span's own bytes, and no person or addressee claim may rest on words the splice does not carry.

rulings.challenge_claim: The declared addressee-shift signal is byte-contested at this onset, the frame addressee being the same second-person-singular hearer on both sides of the 16:9 / 16:10 seam, and the form-class label placed on the answer clause does not match the pointed bytes.
rulings.grounds: Both arms verify at byte tier; the stated severity understates what they reach, so the finding is refined upward. Addressee: לֹא תָב֖וֹא (oshb:Jer.16.8, byte tier) and כִּ֤י תַגִּיד֙ (oshb:Jer.16.10, byte tier) are both second-person-singular forms directed at the same hearer, so no frame-level addressee change stands at the seam, and the plural address in this stretch sits at MT 16:9, before the onset rather than at it. Form class: the clause typed a discourse-frame imperative is וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם (oshb:Jer.16.11, byte tier), a waw-prefixed second-person-singular suffix-conjugation form that both witnesses render as a consequent directive statement rather than a command form; no morphology layer is staged, so the label rests on the pointing, which does not carry it, while the byte exemplars of that signal class at 4:5 and 10:1 are true imperative forms. The same construction stands mid-unit at וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.15.2, byte tier), so the shape alone does not open rows in this book. What lifts this above the stated severity: BOTH declared substrate signals fail on the bytes while the row carries high confidence resting on them, and the substrate-signal field is dependent on the driver -- a failed driver re-opens confidence and the rejected rival with it. The seam itself is not disturbed: the conditional public-question frame opening at MT 16:10 is a real discourse frame and is the ground actually available. Disclosure is clean and is credited (1 marked verse in MT 16:10-16:13, the setumah at MT 16:13, tier-3 weak single-witness; sweep: 0 ketiv/qere notes in MT 16:10-16:13).
rulings.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: drop speech_formula.discourse_imperative and declare instead the signal the onset carries -- the conditional question-and-answer discourse frame opening at 16:10; re-state narrative_frame.addressee_shift at the level the bytes support (the audience of the scripted reply, not the frame hearer, who is second-person singular on both sides) or drop it. boundary_rationale: stop calling the 16:11 clause a discourse-frame imperative and stop drawing the 4:5 / 10:1 comparison for a non-imperative form. confidence: re-open as the dependent field it is -- high is not carried by the corrected signal set. Re-check strongest_rejected_alternative against the swapped driver. No span change. Cure test: the form-class label must be sustainable on the pointed bytes alone, and the declared onset signal must be one that is byte-absent from the verse immediately preceding the seam.

rulings.challenge_claim: The opening at 16:14 has no seam from any of the six ruled tier-1 classes; the cut is driven by the neum-YHWH tag inside its own onset, which is closure corroboration and not a licensed boundary driver.
rulings.grounds: The driver half is upheld and the evidentiary half is refuted on bytes. UPHELD: the row's only declared substrate signal is the postpositive divine formula, and its onset sentence argues that the formula functions there as an onset rather than as a close -- which inverts the ruled reading of a signal that corroborates closure only, and leaves the cut with no declared licensed driver. REFUTED: the claim that no addressee shift accompanies the cut, both sides describing them in the third person, is byte-false. MT 16:11-16:13 is sustained second-person-plural direct address -- וְאַתֶּ֛ם הֲרֵעֹתֶ֥ם (oshb:Jer.16.12, byte tier) and וְהֵטַלְתִּ֣י אֶתְכֶ֗ם (oshb:Jer.16.13, byte tier) -- while MT 16:14-16:15 carries no second-person form anywhere (per-verse read of both verses), closing on third-person-plural reference, וַהֲשִֽׁבֹתִים֙ עַל אַדְמָתָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.16.15, byte tier). A grammatical-person turn therefore stands at exactly the cut; reading 16:14-15 as continuing the reply is not the better-warranted seam on those bytes, and the backward fold proposed with it is not carried. The recurrence evidence offered is defective in its object as well: the onset at לָכֵ֛ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.16.14, byte tier) is a hinneh plus days-are-coming announcement, while MT 16:16 opens on a first-person presentative plus participle, הִנְנִ֨י שֹׁלֵ֜חַ (oshb:Jer.16.16, byte tier) -- a different construction with a different opening form, so nothing recurs byte-for-byte between them; and the announcement formula's own count object stands at 15 verses on MT keys, not the two further sites stated, one of those verses sitting inside the book's single offset zone (oshb:Jer.9.24 = web:Jer.9.25). High severity is not carried.
rulings.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: add the signal the bytes carry at the seam -- the turn out of second-person-plural direct address (16:11-13) into third-person announcement (16:14-15) -- so the cut rests on a licensed class rather than on the postpositive formula. boundary_rationale: re-word the onset sentence so the formula is cited as corroboration standing inside the onset rather than as what makes the cut. Leave span and confidence as they are: the corrected warrant supports the existing seam. Cure test: the declared driver must be a signal whose presence or absence is byte-decidable at the seam verse pair, and every person claim about 16:10-13 must survive a per-verse check of second-person forms.

rulings.challenge_claim: The opening at 16:16 names no seam from any of the six ruled tier-1 classes; the cut from 16:14-15 rests on a change of imagery alone, with no addressee or grammatical-person shift to ground it.
rulings.grounds: The substance is upheld on bytes; two framing elements are wrong. UPHELD: no person or addressee change separates the two sides of this seam. MT 16:15 closes on third-person-plural reference, וַהֲשִֽׁבֹתִים֙ עַל אַדְמָתָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.16.15, byte tier), and MT 16:16 keeps the same third-person-plural referents in the same divine mouth, וְדִיג֑וּם (oshb:Jer.16.16, byte tier), through the recompense clause at עֲוֺנָם֙ וְחַטָּאתָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.16.18, byte tier); no participant, location or hearer changes across the cut, so the declared scene-shift signal is not byte-carried and what actually turns is the imagery, from return-promise to pursuit. That continuity is a byte-true device straddling the row's own opening seam and is nowhere disclosed, which under the cross-seam cohesion rule argues continuity against the cut until the row faces it; and the rival the row actually rejects is only the easier forward pairing with the trust-hymn at 16:19-21, never the backward join that shares mouth, referents and person. CORRECTED FRAMING: the row does name one of the ruled classes -- the defect is that the named class fails on the bytes, not that none is named; and the comparandum offered against it is byte-false, since the onset at MT 16:14 is a hinneh plus days-are-coming announcement while MT 16:16 opens on a first-person presentative plus participle, different constructions with different opening forms. Credited and not disturbed: the one variant note in the span, at MT 16:16 on the fishermen noun (sweep: 1 note in MT 16:16-16:18), is disclosed and correctly located, and the splice stops before it; parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed. Medium stands: both declared signals and the rejected-rival ground are affected while the row carries high confidence.
rulings.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: replace narrative_frame.scene_shift with a signal the bytes carry at 16:16, or hold the seam on disclosed grounds instead -- a content reversal from return-promise to pursuit, with the third-person-plural continuity across the seam disclosed against the row per the cross-seam cohesion rule and the tier-3 mark at MT 16:15 cited as corroboration only, never as driver. strongest_rejected_alternative: rewrite it to test the backward join with 16:14-15 rather than the forward pairing with 16:19-21. confidence: re-open with the driver swap. Merging 16:16-18 into the preceding row is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit owner adoption -- never author work. Cure test: the seam must survive a cross-seam cohesion check with the straddling third-person continuity disclosed, and the rejected rival must be the one the bytes make hardest to reject.

rulings.challenge_claim: The declared signal rests on a person-label the bytes contest, and the gloss extends past the splice to exactly the words that contest it: the span is direct second-person address, not third-person description.
rulings.grounds: Verified from the bytes. The row's 17:1 splice stops at the atnach, and the clause it then glosses as third-person indictment of Judah's altars ends on a second-person-plural suffix, וּלְקַרְנ֖וֹת מִזְבְּחוֹתֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.17.1, byte tier) -- so the glossed words are precisely the ones the splice does not carry and precisely the ones that falsify the label; gloss extent must equal splice extent. Beyond that clause the span stays direct address: MT 17:3 is sustained second-person singular, and MT 17:4 continues second-person singular before closing on a second-person-plural verb inside the row's own quoted close, כִּֽי אֵ֛שׁ קְדַחְתֶּ֥ם (oshb:Jer.17.4, byte tier). Only MT 17:2 is third-person throughout (per-verse read of MT 17:1-17:4). The same byte-false person label is carried a second time in the row's rejected-rival sentence, so the repair is two fields, not one. What the challenge rightly leaves standing: the addressee change at the seam is real, running from praise addressed to the deity at the close of chapter 16 to a directly addressed Judah, so the declared signal class holds and the boundary is untouched; parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 16:21 ahead of the opening, setumah at MT 17:4 at the close; tier-3 weak, single-witness), and no variant note falls in MT 17:1-17:4 (sweep: 0 notes). Low stands: the cure is a wording and splice-extent re-cut with no seam, type or confidence consequence.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'third-person indictment' and 'third-person description' with what the bytes carry -- an addressee turn from praise addressed to the deity to Judah addressed directly, second-person plural at the end of 17:1 and second-person singular through 17:3-17:4 -- and either extend the 17:1 splice to cover the altars clause the gloss claims or cut the gloss back to the spliced words. Leave span, unit_type and confidence unchanged. Cure test: read every splice back inside its own sentence and confirm each person label is carried by words the splice actually contains.

rulings.challenge_claim: The span is typed judgment_oracle under the closed unit_type vocabulary, but the span's own literature-type wording calls the material wisdom-toned, and that operative-category deviation is not disclosed anywhere in device_notes, which addresses only parashah marks.
rulings.grounds: Verified against the row and the bytes. The closed vocabulary carries no wisdom category, so the judgment-oracle type is the defensible closest fit for the curse-and-consequence shape of 17:5-17:8 and the ill-gotten-riches saying at 17:11; the row twice signals that stretch in prose -- in its literature-type wording and in the closing clause of its onset reasoning -- while its disclosure sentences carry only parashah material, so the one-sentence operative-category disclosure the law places in the disclosure field is absent from it. The byte layer is otherwise sound and is credited: the onset at MT 17:5 is a verse-initial divine koh-amar with no quoted-prophet or letter-embedded owner anywhere in the window, so the formula genuinely carries a frame owner; the three-note variant count stated for the span is exact against the staged inventory (MT 17:8, MT 17:10 and MT 17:11 are the only notes between 17:5 and 17:11) and no splice runs through a doubled reading; the parashah statements are correct and correctly typed (setumah at MT 17:4 ahead, setumah at MT 17:6 and MT 17:10 inside, MT 17:11 unmarked; tier-3 weak, single-witness, absence not treated as counterevidence); and the participle at MT 17:7 is read as the passive form rather than the homographic personal name, which is the byte-correct reading. Low stands: the substance is disclosed, in the wrong field. NEW FINDING on the same row, uncharged in the reviews before me: three splices run past the extent of their paired English gloss -- at MT 17:7 the splice continues וְהָיָ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה מִבְטַחֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.17.7, byte tier) past a gloss stopping at the trust clause, at MT 17:10 it continues בֹּחֵ֣ן כְּלָי֑וֹת (oshb:Jer.17.10, byte tier) past a gloss stopping at the searching clause, and MT 17:9 has the same shape -- the gloss-extent rule breached in the opposite direction from the label defect ruled at 17:1-17:4.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add one sentence disclosing the operative-category deviation -- the closed vocabulary has no wisdom category and judgment_oracle is taken as the closest fit for this material -- leaving unit_type a closed-vocabulary value and the free-text literature_type_guess wording as it stands. Separately (new finding): re-cut the three splice/gloss pairs in boundary_rationale at 17:7, 17:9 and 17:10 so each gloss covers exactly what its splice carries, by extending the gloss or trimming the splice. Cure test: unit_type must remain a vocabulary value with the deviation sentence living in device_notes; and every spliced run must read back inside its own sentence with no Hebrew standing beyond the English it is paired with.

supported_sample.claim_checked: the opening-seam warrant at 17:14 and the ground given for declining the backward extension to 17:12-13
supported_sample.notes: The onset claim itself verifies at byte tier: MT 17:14 opens רְפָאֵ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ וְאֵ֣רָפֵ֔א הוֹשִׁיעֵ֖נִי וְאִוָּשֵׁ֑עָה (oshb:Jer.17.14, byte tier) -- imperatives carrying first-person-singular object suffixes with the divine name vocative between them -- against MT 17:13, which describes the forsakers in the third person while addressing the deity, so the speaker-focus turn the row relies on is byte-true and both witnesses render it so. The disclosure layer verifies too: setumah at MT 17:13 ahead of the opening and setumah at MT 17:18 at the close (tier-3 weak, single-witness), and 0 ketiv/qere notes in MT 17:14-17:18, so nothing is owed on that arm. The defect is in what the seam argument omits. MT 17:13 closes its first colon on the shaming verb, כָּל עֹזְבֶ֖יךָ יֵבֹ֑שׁוּ (oshb:Jer.17.13, byte tier), and MT 17:18 opens on the same form, יֵבֹ֤שׁוּ רֹדְפַי֙ (oshb:Jer.17.18, byte tier); the two are identical once cantillation is set aside and differ only by accent, and a skeleton sweep on that attested form returns 5 verses on MT keys, exactly two of them in chapter 17 (identity numbering here -- the book's single offset zone is confined to chapters 8-9 and no digit in this note touches it). That is a byte-true device bracketing 17:13 to 17:18 and straddling this row's own opening seam, which the cross-seam cohesion rule makes owed disclosure, and it argues continuity with 17:12-13 against the cut; the row's rejected-rival sentence sets the backward extension aside without facing it. Work order: disclose the straddling recurrence in the row's cohesion reasoning with its tier named and re-argue the backward rival against it -- extending the span to 17:12 would be a boundary proposal for owner adoption, never author work.
